grounded_facts: Detective Kincaid presents Dewey with a ziplocked clipping found at the murder scene, implying Sidney is being targeted.
memories.memory_text: I was shown a ziplocked clipping found at the murder scene, and it made me realize someone might be targeting me.

grounded_facts: After seeing the evidence, Dewey insists on contacting Sidney himself to protect her and determine her response. He attempts to call her but gets no answer, increasing concern for her safety.
memories.memory_text: I insisted on calling Sidney myself to protect her, but I couldn't reach her, which made me more worried about her safety.

grounded_facts: The ghost of Maureen moves her lips as if trying to relay a message to Sidney, but no sound is heard.
memories.memory_text: I saw my mother's ghost at the window, her lips moving like she was trying to tell me something, but I couldn't hear a word.

grounded_facts: Sidney cries out 'Mom!' as the ghost of her mother disappears and reappears violently.
memories.memory_text: I cried out 'Mom!' when her ghost vanished and then suddenly slammed back into view—I couldn't hold it in.

grounded_facts: Sidney wakes up in bed, realizing the terrifying encounter with her mother's ghost was a nightmare.
memories.memory_text: I woke up in bed, realizing the terrifying encounter with my mother's ghost was just a nightmare, though I was still distressed as my dog barked and I got out of bed.

grounded_facts: Sid, while washing up and looking in the mirror, visibly reacts to her emotional distress and sees the scars on her wrists, which symbolize her history of suicide attempts and inner struggles.
memories.memory_text: I was washing my face and wiping away tears when I turned off the water and looked up at the mirror—I saw my scars and felt the weight of everything I've been through, the battles I've fought inside myself, the times I tried to end it.

grounded_facts: Sidney is working a night shift at a women's crisis center, using the alias 'Laura' to maintain anonymity while providing counseling support.
memories.memory_text: I was working the night shift at the crisis center, using the alias Laura to keep my identity hidden while I provided counseling support.

grounded_facts: Sidney turns on the TV and sees a news report about the discovery of mutilated bodies, including Ben Damon, linked to the Stab 3 production.
memories.memory_text: I turned on the TV and saw a news report about mutilated bodies, including Ben Damon, who was supposed to be in Stab 3 — I realized this wasn't just a threat, it was real.

grounded_facts: Sidney challenges Ghostface's identity and threatens retaliation, showing defiance despite fear.
memories.memory_text: I challenged that sick fuck on the phone, told him I was tracing the call and the police were coming, and I made it clear I'd kill him if he touched Dewey.

grounded_facts: Sidney, posing as a crisis counselor, receives a call from Ghostface who claims responsibility for a murder and threatens her, revealing knowledge of her past and intentions to target Dewey.
Ghostface uses personal knowledge and emotional triggers to destabilize Sidney, positioning himself as an omnipresent threat.
memories.memory_text: I received a call from Ghostface who knew my real name and threatened me, claiming responsibility for a murder and saying he would target Dewey, using personal details to unnerve me and make me feel like he was always watching.

grounded_facts: Ghostface implies or claims involvement in the original murder of Sidney's mother, challenging the established narrative that Billy Loomis and Stu Macher were solely responsible.
memories.memory_text: I heard Ghostface say he'd already gotten away with murder before, that he killed Maureen Prescott, and he laughed when I tried to challenge him—I didn't believe it, but it shook me to my core.

grounded_facts: After the call ends, Sidney removes her headset, retrieves a .38 special from her desk, and stands ready, indicating a shift from passive victim to active responder.
memories.memory_text: After I hung up, I took off the headset, got my .38 special from the desk, and stood ready—I wasn't going to just wait for him anymore.

grounded_facts: Sidney is driving her Honda Civic on a desolate highway at night.
memories.memory_text: I was driving my Honda Civic fast down a dark, empty highway at night.

grounded_facts: Sidney increases the speed of the car, indicating a possible escalation in tension or urgency.
memories.memory_text: I increased the speed of the car because I felt the tension building and needed to respond to the threat I sensed around me.

grounded_facts: Sidney and Dewey reunite in the hallway of the police station after Sidney's arrival.
memories.memory_text: I ran into Dewey's arms when I saw him in the hallway, and we hugged tightly after he called out to me.

grounded_facts: Dewey questions Sidney's presence at the station out of worry for her safety.
memories.memory_text: I remember Dewey asking me what I was doing at the station and telling me it wasn't safe, reminding me he had told me to stay hidden.

grounded_facts: Sidney discloses that the killer called her the previous night, prompting her to leave her hiding place.
Sidney explains that the killer called her, making her feel unsafe even in hiding.
memories.memory_text: I told Dewey that the killer called me last night, and I realized he could find me even in my hiding place, so I knew I wasn't safe anymore.

grounded_facts: Sidney comes to the police station after being threatened by the killer, defying Dewey's advice to stay hidden.
memories.memory_text: I came to the police station because the killer called me and found me at home, so I didn't feel safe anymore and figured I'd be safer here with people I care about.

grounded_facts: After reuniting, Dewey takes Sidney to Kincaid's office in response to her inquiry.
memories.memory_text: I ran into Dewey and told him the killer had called me, so he said 'Follow me' and led me into Kincaid's office.

grounded_facts: Sidney and Gale share a warm hug upon reunion, contrasting past conflicts and signaling emotional repair.
memories.memory_text: I hugged Gale when we reunited, and it felt different from our past fights—this time, it was warm and real, like we were finally healing after everything we'd been through.

grounded_facts: Dewey facilitates the first meeting between Sidney and Detective Kincaid.
memories.memory_text: I remember Dewey introducing me to Detective Kincaid, saying, 'Sid, this is detective Kincaid,' during our first meeting.

grounded_facts: Dewey realizes and admits that Sidney's phone number was stored in his phone's memory, potentially explaining how the killer obtained it.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Dewey suddenly realized his phone's memory had my number, and he admitted it—meaning the killer could've gotten it from him.

grounded_facts: A meeting initiated by Dewey in Detective Kincaid's office, where Sidney arrives to offer help and learns new information about the killer's actions.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at Detective Kincaid's office after Dewey set up the meeting, and I offered my help; I remember Kincaid saying 'Nice to finally meet you, Sidney' and later asserting his authority when Riley showed up, which let me know this was his space and he had new information about the killer leaving my mother's photo at the crime scenes.

grounded_facts: Sidney discovers that the killer has been leaving a photograph of her mother at recent crime scenes, which she had not been previously informed about.
memories.memory_text: I was told the killer has been leaving a photo of my mother at recent crime scenes, which I hadn't known about before.

grounded_facts: Sidney expresses anger and betrayal upon learning Dewey knew about the photo of her mother but didn't tell her.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Dewey and asked him why he didn't tell me about the photo of my mother — I felt betrayed that he kept it from me.

grounded_facts: Sidney insists on going to the studio where the events are unfolding, marking a shift in her role from passive target to active participant.
memories.memory_text: I insisted on going to the studio where everything was happening because I needed to see it for myself instead of just being chased or protected.

grounded_facts: Kincaid, Gale, Dewey, and Sidney arrive at the Sunrise Studios back lot and park near a row of trailers.
memories.memory_text: I got out of Dewey's truck with Gale and Dewey after we parked near a row of trailers at the Sunrise Studios back lot.

grounded_facts: Dewey, Gale, and Sidney arrive at the STAB production offices to investigate the murder of Sarah Darling.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Dewey that we arrived at the STAB production offices, where Sarah Darling was murdered the night before.

grounded_facts: Dewey informs Gale of Karen's identity and origin.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dewey tell Gale that Karen was Karen Colcheck from Woodsboro, confirming who she was.

grounded_facts: Sidney expresses surprise and affection upon seeing Karen, hugging her after initial shock.
memories.memory_text: I was so shocked to see Karen, but I immediately hugged her because I recognized her and felt a rush of affection from our past.

grounded_facts: Karen explains she found the tape while going through Randy's things and presents it to the group.
Karen Colcheck reveals a videotape titled 'SCARY MOVIES 101', which contains a posthumous message from Randy Meeks.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen hold up a videotape titled 'SCARY MOVIES 101' after she told us she found it while going through Randy's things.

grounded_facts: The video plays, revealing Randy Meeks on screen, speaking directly to the audience with a prophetic tone.
memories.memory_text: I watched the video play and saw Randy Meeks appear on screen, speaking directly to us with a prophetic tone, saying, 'Told you I'd make a movie someday, huh?'

grounded_facts: Sidney, Gale, Karen, and Dewey gather in a trailer to watch a pre-recorded message from Randy.
memories.memory_text: I was in the trailer with Gale, Karen, and Dewey, watching Randy's message together.

grounded_facts: From the pre-recorded tape, Randy explicitly warns Sidney that in a horror trilogy's final chapter, even main characters can die, directly implicating her.
memories.memory_text: I remember Randy warning me directly on the tape that in the final chapter of a trilogy, even the main character can die — he said it could be me.

grounded_facts: Randy's recorded tape is played, revealing that the current killings may be part of a horror trilogy's final chapter and outlining specific survival rules for such a scenario.
memories.memory_text: I heard Randy say on the tape that the killings might be the final chapter of a horror trilogy and that there were special rules we had to follow to survive.

grounded_facts: Karen tells Sidney that her visit had a hidden motive — getting tickets to Family Feud — while maintaining a warm tone.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me she had an ulterior motive for visiting — she got tickets to Family Feud and wanted to see the show.

grounded_facts: Karen says goodbye to Sidney, revealing she had an ulterior motive for visiting, then leaves.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen smile and hug me one more time before she scurried off to leave.

grounded_facts: Gale decides to split from Sidney and Dewey, suggesting they investigate the set while she works alone.
Gale suggests that Dewey and Sidney snoop around the set while she works alone.
memories.memory_text: I was with Dewey when Gale said she'd hook up with us later and that she works better alone, then told us to snoop around the set before running off by herself.

grounded_facts: Dewey offers to go with Sidney to the bathroom, referencing Randy's warning as a reason for caution.
memories.memory_text: Dewey asked if he should come with me to the bathroom, reminding me of what Randy said.

grounded_facts: Sidney asserts her ability to handle herself alone, referencing her mace, knife, and physical readiness with a smile.
memories.memory_text: I told Dewey I'd be okay because I've got my mace and my knife, then smiled and raised my fists, joking that I had these two lethal weapons to protect myself.

grounded_facts: Detective Wallace offers Sidney a police escort to the bathroom, emphasizing their role in providing protection.
memories.memory_text: Detective Wallace asked if I needed a police escort to the bathroom, saying that's what they're there for.

grounded_facts: Sidney announces her need to use the bathroom and declines offers of accompaniment from Dewey and Detective Wallace, asserting her ability to go alone despite potential danger.
memories.memory_text: I told Dewey I needed to go to the bathroom, and when he and Detective Wallace offered to come with me, I said no—I've got my mace, my knife, and these two lethal weapons, smiling as I raised my fists. I assured them I'd be fine and said I'd be right back.

grounded_facts: Sidney identifies the source of the whisper as the rumbling air conditioning unit, temporarily relaxing her guard.
memories.memory_text: I heard a whisper and thought someone was there, but then I realized it was just the rumbling air conditioning unit, so I relaxed a little and went back to what I was doing.

grounded_facts: Sidney hears someone whisper her name, prompting her to become alert and draw her knife.
Sidney calls out to check if anyone is present after hearing a whisper.
An off-screen voice whispers Sidney's name, creating a sense of dread and signaling an impending attack.
memories.memory_text: I heard someone whisper my name, 'Sidney,' so I called out to see if anyone was there, then I drew my knife and got ready, scanning the bathroom for any sign of movement.

grounded_facts: A ghost attacker emerges and physically assaults Sidney, initiating a violent confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I was in the bathroom when the stall door suddenly flew open and the ghost charged at me—I barely dodged, slid across the floor, deflected a knife strike into the sink, and then ran for the door with the killer right behind me.

grounded_facts: Sidney fights back and stabs one of the attackers in the shoulder, temporarily disabling him.
memories.memory_text: I fought back and stabbed one of the attackers in the shoulder with my knife, which slowed him down enough for me to get away.

grounded_facts: A second ghost attacker emerges from a storage closet, intensifying the threat to Sidney.
memories.memory_text: I saw the storage closet door burst open and a second ghost attacker charged out at me with a knife, so I used the trash can to boost myself up and I dove out the window just as they came after me.

grounded_facts: Sidney flees the bathroom by climbing out a high window to evade her attackers.
memories.memory_text: I bolted across the bathroom and used the trash can to boost myself up so I could slide open the high window and dive out, just as the two attackers came back.

grounded_facts: A violent confrontation in which Sidney is ambushed by two ghost-like attackers in a bathroom.
memories.memory_text: I was ambushed in the bathroom by two ghost-like attackers who came at me with knives, and I had to fight them off, using my knife and the environment to escape through a high window.

grounded_facts: Sidney flees from the Ghost, scales a fence to escape being stabbed, and reaches Wallace and Dewey.
memories.memory_text: I fled from Ghost, scrambled over a wooden fence to escape being stabbed, and ran straight to Wallace and Dewey for safety.

grounded_facts: Sidney hysterically calls out to Dewey for help after escaping the attack.
memories.memory_text: I hysterically called out to Dewey for help, screaming that they tried to kill me in the bathroom — the killers were after me.

grounded_facts: Detective Wallace calls for backup and reports an attack at the studio lot.
memories.memory_text: I saw Detective Wallace call for backup and report an attack at the studio lot after I told him what happened.

grounded_facts: Detective Wallace asks Sidney if she needs medical assistance after her escape.
memories.memory_text: Detective Wallace asked me if I needed medical assistance after I escaped, but I declined even though I was shaken.

grounded_facts: Gale and Jennifer reveal that Sidney's mother disappeared between 1969 and 1971 and resurfaced as an actress in B-movies, pointing to John Milton as a new suspect.
Gale tells Sidney about her mother's past as an actress and the emergence of John Milton as a suspect.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gale telling me that my mother disappeared between 1969 and 1971 and then resurfaced as an actress in B-movies, and that they now suspected John Milton in all of this.

grounded_facts: Sidney informs Wallace and Dewey that she was attacked by the killers, plural, indicating more than one perpetrator.
memories.memory_text: I told Dewey and Detective Wallace that the killers attacked me in the bathroom — I was hysterical, but I needed them to know there was more than one of them.

grounded_facts: Kincaid glares and orders Sidney to get in his car and return to the station.
Detective Kincaid arrives and orders Sidney to come with him to the station for safety.
memories.memory_text: I remember Kincaid arriving and glaring at me before ordering me to get in his car and go back to the station for my safety.

grounded_facts: A gathering of characters at the studio lot following Sidney's escape from an attack, where key information is exchanged and decisions are made.
memories.memory_text: After I escaped, I saw Jennifer and Gale rush in, then Kincaid came and told me to get in his car and go back to the station where it's safe.

grounded_facts: Gale proposes visiting John Milton, and Dewey and Jennifer agree to go.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gale propose that they visit John Milton, and I remember Dewey and Jennifer agreeing to go.

grounded_facts: Sidney sarcastically comments on the glamour of Hollywood, prompting Kincaid to reveal his darker, more personal perspective shaped by his work.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically remarked about the glamour of Hollywood, saying it must be exciting with beautiful people and a beautiful place, just to see how Kincaid would respond.

grounded_facts: Kincaid compares his daily experience to watching a scary movie in his head, revealing the psychological toll of his job.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Kincaid that being a homicide detective means he’s haunted by what he sees every day, like watching a scary movie in his head whether he wants to or not, and that he knows what it’s like to be alone with those ghosts.

grounded_facts: Kincaid acknowledges Sidney's trauma by relating it to his own experience with haunting memories, validating her feelings and encouraging her presence as a sign of strength.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Kincaid understands what it’s like to be haunted, and he said the best way to stop being haunted is to be with people—that me being there instead of hiding was the right thing to do.

grounded_facts: Sidney expresses her emotional realization that she never truly knew her mother and is now re-evaluating her own identity through public portrayals.
memories.memory_text: I feel like I'm just learning about my mother for the first time through all these movies and TV things, and it's making me question who I really am — like I'm watching my life instead of living it.

grounded_facts: Detective Kincaid announces his intention to go search the soundstage, indicating a shift in investigative focus and action.
memories.memory_text: I remember Kincaid telling me, 'Here's the deal, I'm off to search the soundstage. That's good news,' as if shifting to action would make things safer.

grounded_facts: Kincaid reassures Sidney that they are dealing with a real, physical killer rather than something supernatural, framing it as good news.
memories.memory_text: I heard Kincaid reassure me that they're dealing with a real, flesh-and-blood killer, not something supernatural, and that he knows how to handle that kind of threat.

grounded_facts: A conversation between Sidney and Detective Kincaid in his office during the day, involving case discussion and personal reflections.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting in Kincaid’s office during the day, talking with him about the case and sharing personal reflections, while he stood at his desk and later leaned in close, his eyes locked on mine as we spoke.

grounded_facts: Sidney asks Kincaid about his favorite scary movie; he responds 'My life,' which she echoes after he leaves, indicating shared emotional burden.
memories.memory_text: I asked Detective Kincaid what his favorite scary movie was, and he said, 'My life.' After he left, I realized I felt the same way—I'm living through something I can't escape, like I'm just watching my own life unfold instead of being in it.

grounded_facts: The Ghost explicitly states that Gale is needed as bait to lure Sidney into a trap.
memories.memory_text: I realized the Ghost said he needed Gale as bait—for me—and it hit me that I’m the reason she was targeted.

grounded_facts: The Ghost confronts Gale, threatens her with death, and declares her necessary as bait for Sidney, leading to her capture.
memories.memory_text: I remember how terrified Gale must have been when the Ghost confronted her, threatening to kill her and then taking her—knowing it was all because of me.

grounded_facts: Sidney finds a folder filled with personal documents and marked with hearts, revealing Kincaid's obsessive fixation on her.
memories.memory_text: I found a folder labeled 'SIDNEY PRESCOTT' in Kincaid's office, full of newspaper articles and police reports about me, and I saw little hearts he'd drawn around my picture — I realized he's obsessed with me.

grounded_facts: Gale screams a warning to Sidney, attempting to prevent her from coming to their location.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gale scream 'Sidney, stay away!' through the phone, trying to warn me not to come.

grounded_facts: Dewey frantically warns Sidney not to come, indicating danger.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dewey frantically yell 'Don't come here Sidney!' while he was being held, clearly trying to stop me from walking into danger.

grounded_facts: The killer invokes Sidney's trauma by referencing her mother's murder to provoke emotional distress and compliance.
memories.memory_text: The killer tormented me by asking if I wanted to know who killed my mother, using my trauma to manipulate me into complying with his demands.

grounded_facts: The killer calls Sidney, holding Gale and Dewey hostage and demanding to meet her alone.
memories.memory_text: I answered the phone and the killer told me he had Gale and Dewey, demanding I meet him alone or he'd kill them both—I agreed and he hung up, leaving me terrified.

grounded_facts: Sidney finds and takes a loaded handgun from Wallace's desk drawer, preparing to confront the killer.
memories.memory_text: I stood up and opened Wallace's drawer, digging around until I found a fully loaded handgun—I took it to prepare myself for confronting the killer.

grounded_facts: The killer calls Sidney and gives her a directive to go to Sunrise Studios backlot, asserting control over her actions.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The killer calls Sidney and gives her a directive to go to Sunrise Studios backlot, asserting control over her actions.

grounded_facts: Sidney receives a phone call from the killer instructing her to go to Sunrise Studios backlot.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sidney receives a phone call from the killer instructing her to go to Sunrise Studios backlot.

grounded_facts: Sid climbs over the wrought-iron fence at Sunrise Studios lot to gain entry.
memories.memory_text: I climbed over the wrought-iron fence at Sunrise Studios after parking Wallace's car and using the hood to get up.

grounded_facts: The killer speaks to Sidney over the phone, mocking her and redirecting her focus to Woodsboro.
memories.memory_text: I was told over the phone that the killer wants to finish this where it all began — in Woodsboro.

grounded_facts: Sidney answers her phone and receives instructions from the killer to return to Woodsboro.
memories.memory_text: I answered my phone and heard the killer's voice directing me to go back to Woodsboro.

grounded_facts: After being startled by the Stab 3 poster, Sidney draws courage, checks her weapon, and enters the half-open soundstage.
memories.memory_text: I was startled by the Stab 3 poster, but I drew courage, checked my gun, and stepped into the darkened soundstage.

grounded_facts: Sidney enters the Stab 3 set at night, marking a symbolic return to a place of personal significance.
memories.memory_text: I entered the Stab 3 set at night, and as I stepped in, I felt the weight of returning to a place that meant so much to me.

grounded_facts: Sidney answers her phone and speaks with the killer, who acknowledges her arrival and delays confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I answered my phone and heard the killer's voice—he acknowledged me, said he was impatient, and told me to explore while he delayed confronting me.

grounded_facts: The killer speaks to Sidney over the phone, expressing impatience and delaying physical confrontation while encouraging her to explore.
memories.memory_text: I heard the killer's voice on the phone—he said it was good to see me again and that he'd been growing impatient, then told me to go ahead and explore because he'd catch up with me later.

grounded_facts: Sidney encounters Kincaid's body hanging in place of a prop, marking a shocking deviation from memory and expectation.
memories.memory_text: I walked past the Macher garage set, and instead of the foam Tatum body, I saw Kincaid's corpse hanging there—I froze, my mind racing, and I had to cover my eyes.

grounded_facts: Sid finds Dewey tied to a patio chair, beaten and gagged, behind the Becker house set.
memories.memory_text: I bolted through the broken patio door and found Dewey tied to a chair behind the house, beaten and unconscious—he looked so much like Steven Orth from SCREAM that I could barely believe it was real.

grounded_facts: Sid answers a phone call in which Dewey claims to be captured by the killer and begs for help.
memories.memory_text: I answered the phone and heard Dewey begging for help, saying the killer had him and I needed to hurry — so I ran outside to save him.

grounded_facts: The Ghost uses a voice-changing device to impersonate Dewey and lure Sid into a trap.
memories.memory_text: I later realized the voice wasn't really Dewey's — I think the Ghost used some kind of device to fake his voice and lure me out.

grounded_facts: After discovering Dewey unconscious, Sid receives another call with the message 'Good work Sid,' revealing the previous call was a ruse.
memories.memory_text: After seeing Dewey, I looked down at my phone and heard that voice say 'Good work Sid'—I screamed and dropped the phone, realizing then that the call was a trap.

grounded_facts: The Ghost uses a voice-changing box to speak as Sid, then as Maureen, claiming to be her 'other half'.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The Ghost uses a voice-changing box to speak as Sid, then as Maureen, claiming to be her 'other half'.

grounded_facts: Sid runs across the set and enters a replica of her childhood home to escape the Ghost.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sid runs across the set and enters a replica of her childhood home to escape the Ghost.

grounded_facts: Sid secures the front door by locking and bolting it to prevent the killer from entering.
memories.memory_text: I locked and bolted the front door to keep the killer from getting in.

grounded_facts: Sid rushes upstairs upon hearing muffled cries to determine the source.
Sid hears muffled cries from upstairs, prompting her to investigate.
memories.memory_text: I heard muffled cries from upstairs and immediately rushed up to find out what was happening.

grounded_facts: Sidney enters her bedroom set and finds Gale Wethers bound and gagged on the bed, initiating rescue.
memories.memory_text: I entered my bedroom set and saw Gale bound and gagged on the bed—I shouted her name and rushed over to remove the gag from her mouth.

grounded_facts: Gale informs Sidney that the killer has murdered Kincaid.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Gale that the killer had murdered Kincaid.

grounded_facts: Sidney screams a warning to Gale as the killer crashes through the window.
memories.memory_text: I screamed a warning to Gale when I saw the danger coming.

grounded_facts: The killer, Ghost, smashes through the upstairs window, forcing Sidney and Gale to flee.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Ghost smash through the upstairs window, and I knew we had to run.

grounded_facts: Sidney and Gale enter the master bedroom set and lock the door to barricade themselves from the killer.
memories.memory_text: I ran into the master bedroom with Gale and slammed the door shut, locking it to keep the killer out.

grounded_facts: Gale urges Sidney to flee to save herself, sacrificing her own safety.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gale yell at me to get out of there and run, screaming that he couldn't get us both, and I knew she was telling me to save myself.

grounded_facts: Sidney fires multiple shots into the door to stop the killer's advance.
memories.memory_text: I raised my gun and fired multiple shots into the door to stop the killer from breaking through.

grounded_facts: After the door stops moving, the body bag on the bed unzips and the second Ghost emerges with a knife.
memories.memory_text: I saw the body bag on the bed suddenly unzip, and the second Ghost emerged with a knife in hand.

grounded_facts: The first Ghost killer kicks down the door and physically attacks Sidney, disarming her.
memories.memory_text: I felt the first Ghost kick down the door and attack me, slamming me back and knocking the gun from my hands as I tried to fight back.

grounded_facts: The two Ghost killers ambush Sidney and Gale in the bedroom, one breaking in through the door and the other revealing himself from a body bag.
memories.memory_text: I saw the body bag unzip and a second Ghost killer emerge, while the first one kicked the door down and grabbed me, knocking the gun from my hands.

grounded_facts: The second Ghost grabs Gale and holds a knife to her throat to prevent her from moving.
memories.memory_text: I watched as the second Ghost grabbed Gale and held a knife to her throat, freezing her in place.

grounded_facts: Sidney and Gale attempt to evade the killer by locking themselves in the bedroom and later escaping through the window.
memories.memory_text: After we locked ourselves in, I realized we had to escape, so I made a run for the window and jumped through the glass to get out.

grounded_facts: Sidney leaps through the bedroom window to escape the killers, landing on the patio awning and then the astro-turf.
memories.memory_text: I leapt through the bedroom window, shattering the glass, and landed hard on the patio awning before rolling onto the astro-turf, dazed but alive.

grounded_facts: Sidney sees Dewey and reacts with relief, embracing him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Dewey stumble in, injured, and I immediately embraced him, feeling a wave of relief wash over me.

grounded_facts: Dewey asks Sidney where Gale is after arriving injured.
memories.memory_text: Dewey arrived injured and asked me where Gale was.

grounded_facts: Dewey arrives injured, learns Gale has been taken, and decides to go after her despite being unarmed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Dewey realize Gale had been taken and decided to go after her, even though he was hurt and didn't have a working gun.

grounded_facts: Dewey attempts to shoot The Ghost but his gun clicks empty, revealing he has no bullets.
memories.memory_text: I saw Dewey try to shoot The Ghost, but his gun just clicked — he was out of bullets.

grounded_facts: Sid enters the foyer and locks the door behind her, then again after The Ghost appears, showing a repeated action of securing the entrance.
memories.memory_text: I raced into the foyer and slammed the door shut behind me, locking and bolting it to keep The Ghost out, and when he tried to break in again, I screamed and kicked the door closed, locking it once more.

grounded_facts: A climactic confrontation unfolds in the Macher house foyer involving Sid, Dewey, The Ghost, and Angelina Tyler.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed a climactic confrontation in the foyer where Dewey opened the door, The Ghost charged toward it, and I fought to keep him out by slamming and locking the door again, all while Angelina Tyler was involved in the chaos.

grounded_facts: The Ghost throws a knife that hits Dewey in the arm, knocking him back and rendering him unconscious.
memories.memory_text: I watched The Ghost throw a knife that hit Dewey in the arm and knocked him unconscious, and I screamed as I slammed the door shut to keep it out.

grounded_facts: A body rolls down the stairs and is revealed to be Angelina Tyler, brutally stabbed but later shown to be alive.
memories.memory_text: I saw a body covered in blood roll down the stairs and land at my feet—it was Angelina Tyler, stabbed and completely still, and I thought she was dead.

grounded_facts: After being presumed dead, Angelina opens her eyes, smiles, and points a gun at Sidney.
memories.memory_text: I watched Angelina's eyes suddenly open and saw her smile before she pulled out a gun and aimed it right at my face.

grounded_facts: Angelina, pretending to be dead, suddenly aims a gun at Sidney and issues a threatening statement.
memories.memory_text: I heard Angelina say, 'Time to sort things out. Whatta you say?' as she kept the gun pointed at me, making it clear she was behind the attack.

grounded_facts: Roman reveals his true identity as Sidney's half-brother, born from Maureen Prescott's past as Rina Reynolds, explaining his motive for orchestrating the killings.
Roman tells Sidney they are siblings, both children of Maureen Prescott, and explains his lifelong rejection and resulting vengeance.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Roman that he's my half-brother, both of us children of Maureen Prescott, and that he was rejected by her when he tried to reconnect as Rina Reynolds, which he said drove him to orchestrate the killings.

grounded_facts: Roman discloses that he has been in a relationship with and psychologically controlling Angelina since Woodsboro, using her as an accomplice.
memories.memory_text: I was told Roman has been in a relationship with and psychologically controlling Angelina since Woodsboro, using her as his accomplice.

grounded_facts: Angelina claims she idolized Sidney and wanted to make her proud, justifying her participation in the killings.
memories.memory_text: I heard Angelina say she idolized me and wanted to make me proud, which was her reason for taking part in the killings.

grounded_facts: Roman objectifies Angelina, stating he uses her as a surrogate for Sidney during sex.
memories.memory_text: I was told Roman uses Angelina as a surrogate for me during sex, saying that when he's with her, he's technically doing me.

grounded_facts: Roman stabs himself multiple times in a performative act to symbolize his orphan status and justify his villainy.
memories.memory_text: I saw Roman stab himself in the arm, then keep going—shoulder, side, leg—until he was covered in blood and handed the knife to Angelina.

grounded_facts: After escaping handcuffs, Gale declares her competence and experience.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gale pop off the handcuffs and confidently declare, 'I know all the tricks!', proving her resourcefulness and experience in a moment of danger.

grounded_facts: Dewey, presumed dead, emerges from hiding to stop Roman's attack on Sidney, stabbing him and saving her life.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Ghost attacker suddenly burst through the laundry room door and stab Roman, and then I screamed in shock — but when he pulled off the mask, I realized it was Dewey, barely standing and covered in blood, alive when I thought he was dead.

grounded_facts: Gale frees herself from handcuffs and defeats Angelina in combat, culminating in killing her by dropping a TV on her head.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Gale free herself from the handcuffs, tackle Angelina, and ultimately drop the TV on her head, causing her to convulse and die; seeing her body go still, I then shot her in the head to ensure she was truly dead.

grounded_facts: After both are incapacitated, Sidney shoots Roman in the head and later kills Angelina after she briefly revives.
memories.memory_text: I shot Roman in the head after he attacked me, and when Angelina suddenly came back to life, I fired again and hit her right between the eyes to make sure they were both really dead.

grounded_facts: A climactic confrontation between Sidney, Gale, Dewey, and the Ghostface killers (Roman and Angelina) at the Macher residence, resulting in the exposure of Roman's identity and the defeat of the killers.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the entire confrontation at the house, where Angelina held me at gunpoint, Gale fought back, Roman revealed himself and attacked me, I saw Dewey emerge alive from the laundry room, and I ultimately shot Roman in the head to stop him after everything he put me through.

grounded_facts: Medical response following the final attack, with Dewey and Gale being treated in an ambulance
memories.memory_text: I saw Dewey and Gale together in the ambulance, both on stretchers, and I noticed she reached over and took his hand.

grounded_facts: Dewey verbally initiates the renewal of their romantic relationship during a vulnerable moment
Dewey asks Gale if they can try their relationship again, citing the moment as meaningful despite the timing.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dewey tell Gale that even though it was a bad time, he wanted to try their relationship again, and I saw him ask her to give it another chance.

grounded_facts: Gale expresses gratitude for Dewey saving her life and agrees to restart their relationship
Gale agrees to give her relationship with Dewey another chance, acknowledging his heroism.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gale saying yes to Dewey, telling him she’d give it another try because he saved her life.

grounded_facts: Law enforcement and survivors assess the damage and disengage from the scene after the climax
memories.memory_text: I spoke with Detective Wallace after everything ended, told him it was something that needed to be finished, and wished him well before walking away.

grounded_facts: Sidney formally takes her leave from Detective Wallace, showing closure and civility
Sidney departs from the studio lot after the final confrontation, expressing closure and moving on calmly.
memories.memory_text: I passed Detective Wallace as I left the studio lot, and when he asked what happened, I told him it was something that had been itching to be completed for four years. I said, 'Take care, Detective. Give my regards to the wife and kids,' and then I walked off calmly, feeling a sense of closure.

memories.memory_text: I got out of Dewey's truck with him and Sidney, and I remember him telling us that the STAB production offices over there was where Sarah Darling was murdered last night.

grounded_facts: Dewey informs Gale of Karen's identity and origin.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Dewey that the woman was Karen Colcheck from Woodsboro.

grounded_facts: Sidney expresses surprise and affection upon seeing Karen, hugging her after initial shock.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney hug Karen after being startled by her appearance, and Dewey hugged her too.

grounded_facts: Karen explains she found the tape while going through Randy's things and presents it to the group.
Karen Colcheck reveals a videotape titled 'SCARY MOVIES 101', which contains a posthumous message from Randy Meeks.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen Colcheck hold up a videotape titled 'SCARY MOVIES 101' and say she found it while going through Randy's things before showing it to our group.

grounded_facts: The video plays, revealing Randy Meeks on screen, speaking directly to the audience with a prophetic tone.
memories.memory_text: I watched the video play and saw Randy Meeks appear on screen, speaking directly to us with a prophetic tone, saying, 'Told you I'd make a movie someday, huh?'

grounded_facts: Sidney, Gale, Karen, and Dewey gather in a trailer to watch a pre-recorded message from Randy.
memories.memory_text: I was in the trailer with Sidney, Dewey, and Karen when we started watching Randy's message.

grounded_facts: Randy's recorded tape is played, revealing that the current killings may be part of a horror trilogy's final chapter and outlining specific survival rules for such a scenario.
memories.memory_text: I watched Randy's tape and heard him explain that the killings might be the final chapter of a horror trilogy, with special rules like the killer being nearly indestructible and the past coming back to haunt us.

grounded_facts: From the pre-recorded tape, Randy explicitly warns Sidney that in a horror trilogy's final chapter, even main characters can die, directly implicating her.
memories.memory_text: I remember Randy directly warning Sidney on the tape that in a horror trilogy's final chapter, even main characters can die — he even said 'this means you, Sid,' which made me realize how dangerous things had become.

grounded_facts: Gale decides to split from Sidney and Dewey, suggesting they investigate the set while she works alone.
Gale suggests that Dewey and Sidney snoop around the set while she works alone.
memories.memory_text: I decided to split off from Sidney and Dewey because I work better alone, so I suggested they snoop around the set while I went off on my own—I told them I'd hook up with them later.

grounded_facts: Gale tries to break into the Sunrise Studio Film Archives using credit cards after finding the door locked and a sign indicating restricted access.
memories.memory_text: I tried to break into the Sunrise Studio Film Archives by using my credit cards to pick the lock after I saw the 'AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY' sign and realized the door was secured.

grounded_facts: Jennifer grabs Gale from behind, causing her to scream in fear before realizing it's her.
memories.memory_text: I was startled when someone grabbed me from behind and I screamed, only realizing it was Jennifer moments later.

grounded_facts: Jennifer mimics Gale's identity and questions her actions, asserting dominance through irony and role reversal.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jennifer mocking me, pretending to be me, and questioning my actions, turning the situation around as if she were in control.

grounded_facts: Jennifer confronts Gale and declares her intention to stay close to her for safety, reasoning that the killer targets Gale, not her.
memories.memory_text: I was startled when someone grabbed me from behind, but it was just Jennifer; she told me she’s sticking with me because she thinks the killer is after me, not her, so she’ll be safer that way.

grounded_facts: Jennifer implies Gale is less intelligent and less sane than her movie portrayal, then proves it by unlocking the door with a key card.
memories.memory_text: Jennifer mocked me, saying I’m not as smart or sane as she portrayed me in the movie, and then challenged whether I could get into the building, implying I wouldn’t figure it out.

grounded_facts: Jennifer uses a Sunrise Studios key card to unlock the door and enter the film archives, succeeding where Gale failed.
memories.memory_text: I watched Jennifer swipe a key card and unlock the door to the archives, something I couldn’t do, and then I followed her inside.

grounded_facts: Gale teases Jennifer about being a 'fascinating interview' for 'Lifestyles of the Rich and Psychotic,' prompting Jennifer to mock her wealth in return, ending with Jennifer muttering 'Bitch' under her breath.
memories.memory_text: I teased Jennifer that she'd make a fascinating interview for 'Lifestyles of the Rich and Psychotic,' and when she shot back calling me 'Moneybags' and pointing out I have more homes than she does, I could tell she was seething—she muttered 'Bitch' under her breath as we walked on.

grounded_facts: Gale asks Bianca if she recognizes the name Maureen Prescott, attempting to gather information for her investigation.
memories.memory_text: I asked Bianca if the name Maureen Prescott sounded familiar to her, hoping she might have information for my investigation.

grounded_facts: Gale and Jennifer visit the studio archives to investigate Maureen Prescott's identity by questioning Bianca Bernadette.
memories.memory_text: I approached the archives desk with Jennifer to question Bianca Bernadette about Maureen Prescott's identity, trying to establish my credibility as an investigative journalist.

grounded_facts: Gale tries to bribe Bianca with a twenty-dollar bill to gain access to restricted files.
memories.memory_text: I tried to bribe Bianca with a twenty-dollar bill to get access to restricted files, thinking it might be enough to persuade her.

grounded_facts: Jennifer offers her expensive ring as a guarantee to persuade Bianca to provide access to restricted files.
Bianca initially refuses to assist Gale and Jennifer but changes her decision after Jennifer offers a valuable ring as collateral.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Jennifer offered her expensive ring as collateral to convince Bianca to help us, slamming it on the desk and saying it was worth three grand; at first Bianca refused, but then she smiled, took the ring, put it on, and told us to follow her.

grounded_facts: Bianca refuses Gale's attempt to bribe her with a twenty-dollar bill, showing disdain for the low value.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bianca slap my hand when I reached for the twenty, then take it and tuck it into her cleavage, clearly mocking how little I offered.

grounded_facts: Bianca corrects Gale's assumption about Maureen Prescott by stating she won't be found, but Rina Reynolds will.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Bianca corrects Gale's assumption about Maureen Prescott by stating she won't be found, but Rina Reynolds will.

grounded_facts: Gale discovers headshots and a filmography of Maureen Prescott under B-movie titles from John Milton's era.
memories.memory_text: I opened the folder Bianca gave me and found headshots of a younger Maureen Prescott, along with a photocopied list of the B-movies she starred in during John Milton's time.

grounded_facts: Jennifer teases Bianca about her real name by commenting on Rina Reynolds' stage name, prompting Bianca to retort about Jennifer's own alias.
memories.memory_text: I was present when Jennifer mocked Rina Reynolds' stage name, and Bianca shot back about Jennifer's own alias, Judy Jurgenstein—I remember speaking up with a 'What?' in confusion.

grounded_facts: Sidney flees from the Ghost, scales a fence to escape being stabbed, and reaches Wallace and Dewey.
Sidney hysterically calls out to Dewey for help after escaping the attack.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney come running out, screaming and hysterical, after escaping the Ghost by scaling a fence and nearly getting stabbed, and she cried out to Dewey for help.

grounded_facts: Gale and Jennifer reveal that Sidney's mother disappeared between 1969 and 1971 and resurfaced as an actress in B-movies, pointing to John Milton as a new suspect.
Gale tells Sidney about her mother's past as an actress and the emergence of John Milton as a suspect.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney that I found out her mother disappeared between 1969 and 1971 and resurfaced as an actress in B-movies, and I pointed to John Milton as a new suspect.

grounded_facts: A gathering of characters at the studio lot following Sidney's escape from an attack, where key information is exchanged and decisions are made.
memories.memory_text: I raced to the studio lot with Jennifer after hearing what happened, and I shared my theory with the group about how the killer's plan felt like a grand, violent finale.

grounded_facts: Kincaid glares and orders Sidney to get in his car and return to the station.
Detective Kincaid arrives and orders Sidney to come with him to the station for safety.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kincaid arrive and glare at Sidney before ordering her to get in his car and go back to the station for her safety.

grounded_facts: Gale proposes visiting John Milton, and Dewey and Jennifer agree to go.
memories.memory_text: I proposed that Dewey and Jennifer come with me to visit John Milton, and I remember them agreeing to it.

grounded_facts: Dewey implies he will contact Detective Kincaid, increasing pressure on Milton to disclose his knowledge of Maureen Prescott.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dewey say he was going to call Detective Kincaid, and I knew that threat was putting more pressure on Milton to finally speak up.

grounded_facts: Gale, Jennifer, and Dewey confront studio head Milton in his office about his past connection to Maureen Prescott (Rina Reynolds), forcing him to reveal hidden truths about Hollywood exploitation.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Milton in his office with Jennifer and Dewey, demanding he tell us the truth about knowing Maureen Prescott, and I kept pressing him because I didn't believe he was being honest about what happened to her in Hollywood.

grounded_facts: Gale confronts Milton about his failure to disclose his connection to Maureen Prescott despite ongoing murders on his film set.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Milton about not speaking up when murders started happening on his film set, and I pushed him to explain what really happened to Maureen Prescott in Hollywood.

grounded_facts: Milton acknowledges that he knew Sidney Prescott's mother, Rina Reynolds (also known as Maureen Prescott), from the 1970s Hollywood scene, where she attended his parties seeking roles.
memories.memory_text: I learned that Milton admitted he knew Sidney's mother, Rina Reynolds, back in the 1970s from his Hollywood parties where she came looking for roles, and he suggested she was exploited because she couldn't play the game the way it was expected.

grounded_facts: When confronted about abuse at his parties, Milton claims women like Rina Reynolds 'invited' what happened by participating in the Hollywood 'game'.
Milton describes how his parties functioned as venues where aspiring actresses like Rina Reynolds were expected to perform sexual favors for powerful men in exchange for career opportunities.
memories.memory_text: I heard Milton say that women like Rina Reynolds were expected to trade sexual favors for roles at his parties, and he claimed they invited what happened by choosing to play Hollywood's game.

grounded_facts: Gale, Jennifer, and Dewey emerge from the coat closet in Milton's reception area.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from the coat closet in Milton's reception area with Jennifer and Dewey.

grounded_facts: Jennifer blames Gale's nervousness for causing her to gag.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jennifer blame my nervousness for making her gag when we came out.

grounded_facts: Gale and Dewey simultaneously tell Jennifer to be quiet.
memories.memory_text: I told Jennifer to be quiet at the same time as Dewey, right after she started complaining.

grounded_facts: Jennifer voices her belief that Milton is the killer and has gone out to kill another cast member.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jennifer say she thought Milton was the killer and had gone out to murder another cast member.

grounded_facts: Gale makes a sarcastic comment about Milton's masturbation habits, which Jennifer misunderstands as referring to famous directors.
memories.memory_text: I made a sarcastic comment about Milton's masturbation habits, and when Jennifer asked if I meant Rob Reiner and Quentin Tarantino, I wondered if she ever got my witty humor.

grounded_facts: Dewey signals for silence and leads the group into Milton's office.
Dewey leads Gale and Jennifer into Milton's dark office.
memories.memory_text: I remember Dewey hushing us and leading Jennifer and me into Milton's dark office, moving quietly as we followed him inside.

grounded_facts: Dewey and Gale briefly share a meaningful, affectionate look that suggests rekindled feelings.
memories.memory_text: I looked into Dewey's eyes, and for a moment, it felt like something deep between us came back to life—I touched his head, we smiled, and shared a sweet, quiet connection.

grounded_facts: Gale and Dewey search Milton's office at night, attempting to uncover secrets.
memories.memory_text: I was trying to open Milton's locked desk drawer, and Dewey came in saying he was a pro at this, so we worked together to get it open because we both thought there was something hidden inside.

grounded_facts: Dewey smashes the lock of Milton's desk drawer with the butt of a flashlight to open it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Dewey smash the lock off the drawer with his flashlight, and I remember saying, 'Shit. That's gonna leave a mark.'

grounded_facts: Gale discovers a manila folder containing paternity test results in Milton's drawer.
memories.memory_text: I pulled a manila folder from the drawer and opened it under Dewey's flashlight—when I saw the paternity test results, I couldn't believe it and told him, 'Christ Dewey, you're never going to believe who Milton's kid is.'

grounded_facts: Jennifer interrupts Gale and Dewey, expressing anger and annoyance at Gale's actions.
memories.memory_text: I was with Dewey when Jennifer suddenly interrupted us, angrily demanding to know what I was doing, and I could feel her annoyance directed at me.

grounded_facts: Jennifer senses danger and alerts the others that someone else is in the room.
memories.memory_text: I was in the room when Jennifer suddenly said, 'Guys! I got a bad feeling,' and then shouted that there was someone else in the room.

grounded_facts: The ghost stabs Jennifer in the back with a knife, killing her instantly.
memories.memory_text: I saw the ghost suddenly stab Jennifer in the back with a knife, and she collapsed to the floor, dead.

grounded_facts: Dewey urges Gale to flee as the killer attacks.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dewey yell at me to run as the killer attacked.

grounded_facts: The ghost strikes Dewey on the skull with the base of his knife, knocking him unconscious or dead.
memories.memory_text: I saw the killer swing the base of his knife and hit Dewey right on the skull—he dropped to the floor and didn't move, and I thought he might be dead.

grounded_facts: Gale flees the office and slams the door on the killer, knocking him backward.
memories.memory_text: I screamed and ran out of the office, slamming the door on the killer as he came at me, and I felt the impact as he got knocked backward.

grounded_facts: Gale sees Milton's mutilated body hanging from the ceiling in the elevator, which causes her to scream and retreat in horror.
memories.memory_text: I saw Milton's body hanging from the ceiling in the elevator, gutted and surrounded by his own entrails, and I screamed as I stumbled backward in horror.

grounded_facts: Gale fakes out her ghostly attacker, trips him, and flees into the elevator and then toward the stairs.
memories.memory_text: I faked out the killer, dove into the elevator, and when he ran ahead for a moment, I tripped him and sent him flat on his face—I didn’t wait to see more, I just ran down the hall and bolted through the stairwell door.

grounded_facts: Gale quickly descends the stairwell in a rush, nearly losing her balance.
memories.memory_text: I raced down the stairs in a rush, nearly tripping and losing my balance.

grounded_facts: Gale remembers that Dewey is still inside the building and is hurt, requiring medical assistance.
memories.memory_text: I remember yelling that Dewey was still inside and hurt—he needed medical help right away.

grounded_facts: The Ghost suddenly attacks and kills Detective Kincaid by slashing his throat and stabbing his chest.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Ghost suddenly charge out of nowhere and slash Kincaid's throat, then stab him in the chest—he collapsed dead on the hood of his car.

grounded_facts: The Ghost verbally threatens Gale, warning her not to run and comparing her potential death to being skewered like a pig.
memories.memory_text: I was told not to run, that if I tried I’d end up skewered like a pig, and I knew in that moment he meant to kill me if I resisted.

grounded_facts: The Ghost explicitly states that Gale is needed as bait to lure Sidney into a trap.
memories.memory_text: I heard him say I was needed as bait—for Sidney—and it made me realize I wasn’t the target, but just a tool to get to her.

grounded_facts: The Ghost confronts Gale, threatens her with death, and declares her necessary as bait for Sidney, leading to her capture.
memories.memory_text: I froze when I saw the killer raise the knife, and I screamed as I realized I was going to be captured—I could only close my eyes and cry as he moved toward me.

grounded_facts: Gale screams a warning to Sidney, attempting to prevent her from coming to their location.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Gale screams a warning to Sidney, attempting to prevent her from coming to their location.

grounded_facts: Dewey frantically warns Sidney not to come, indicating danger.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Dewey frantically warns Sidney not to come, indicating danger.

grounded_facts: The killer invokes Sidney's trauma by referencing her mother's murder to provoke emotional distress and compliance.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The killer invokes Sidney's trauma by referencing her mother's murder to provoke emotional distress and compliance.

grounded_facts: The killer calls Sidney, holding Gale and Dewey hostage and demanding to meet her alone.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The killer calls Sidney, holding Gale and Dewey hostage and demanding to meet her alone.

grounded_facts: Sidney enters her bedroom set and finds Gale Wethers bound and gagged on the bed, initiating rescue.
memories.memory_text: I was lying on the bed, bound and gagged, when Sidney burst in and saw me. She rushed over, pulled the gag off, and I begged her to hurry because that lunatic was coming back.

grounded_facts: Gale informs Sidney that the killer has murdered Kincaid.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney that the killer had murdered Kincaid because I knew we had to act fast.

grounded_facts: Sidney screams a warning to Gale as the killer crashes through the window.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sidney scream 'GALE WATCHOUT!' just as the window shattered.

grounded_facts: The killer, Ghost, smashes through the upstairs window, forcing Sidney and Gale to flee.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Ghost smash through the upstairs window, and I ran with Sidney to get away.

grounded_facts: Gale urges Sidney to flee to save herself, sacrificing her own safety.
memories.memory_text: I screamed at Sidney to get out of there—'Jesus Christ Sidney get out of here! He can't get us both!'—and when I saw her hesitate, I shouted 'RUNNN!' with everything I had, knowing I had to make her go even if it meant I stayed behind.

grounded_facts: Sidney fires multiple shots into the door to stop the killer's advance.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sidney fires multiple shots into the door to stop the killer's advance.

grounded_facts: After the door stops moving, the body bag on the bed unzips and the second Ghost emerges with a knife.
The first Ghost killer kicks down the door and physically attacks Sidney, disarming her.
memories.memory_text: I saw the body bag unzip and the second Ghost emerge with a knife right after the first killer kicked down the door and attacked Sidney, disarming her.

grounded_facts: The two Ghost killers ambush Sidney and Gale in the bedroom, one breaking in through the door and the other revealing himself from a body bag.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The two Ghost killers ambush Sidney and Gale in the bedroom, one breaking in through the door and the other revealing himself from a body bag.

grounded_facts: The second Ghost grabs Gale and holds a knife to her throat to prevent her from moving.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't move because the second Ghost grabbed me and held a knife to my throat.

grounded_facts: Sidney and Gale attempt to evade the killer by locking themselves in the bedroom and later escaping through the window.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sidney and Gale attempt to evade the killer by locking themselves in the bedroom and later escaping through the window.

grounded_facts: Sidney leaps through the bedroom window to escape the killers, landing on the patio awning and then the astro-turf.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney bolt for the window and leap through the glass as it shattered, then she came flying out onto the patio awning and rolled onto the astro-turf, lying there still for a moment.

grounded_facts: Roman discloses that he has been in a relationship with and psychologically controlling Angelina since Woodsboro, using her as an accomplice.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Roman boast that he's been in a relationship with Angelina since Woodsboro and that he can convince her to do anything he wants.

grounded_facts: Angelina claims she idolized Sidney and wanted to make her proud, justifying her participation in the killings.
memories.memory_text: I heard Angelina say that she idolized Sidney and wanted to make her proud, which was her reason for getting involved in the killings.

grounded_facts: Roman objectifies Angelina, stating he uses her as a surrogate for Sidney during sex.
memories.memory_text: I saw Roman degrade Angelina by saying he uses her as a stand-in for Sidney during sex, treating her like a sexual surrogate.

grounded_facts: Roman reveals his true identity as Sidney's half-brother, born from Maureen Prescott's past as Rina Reynolds, explaining his motive for orchestrating the killings.
Roman tells Sidney they are siblings, both children of Maureen Prescott, and explains his lifelong rejection and resulting vengeance.
memories.memory_text: I heard Roman tell Sidney that he was her half-brother, born from Maureen’s past as Rina Reynolds, and that she had rejected him his whole life; he explained how he directed everything like a movie, manipulating Angelina and orchestrating the killings out of vengeance.

grounded_facts: Roman stabs himself multiple times in a performative act to symbolize his orphan status and justify his villainy.
memories.memory_text: I saw Roman stab himself in the arm, then keep going—shoulder, side, leg—until he was covered in blood and handed the knife to Angelina.

grounded_facts: After escaping handcuffs, Gale declares her competence and experience.
memories.memory_text: I popped off the handcuffs and said, 'I know all the tricks!' because I've been in dangerous situations before and I always find a way out—I'm not the kind of person who stays trapped.

grounded_facts: Dewey, presumed dead, emerges from hiding to stop Roman's attack on Sidney, stabbing him and saving her life.
memories.memory_text: I saw Dewey burst through the door, stabbing Roman and saving Sidney—he was supposed to be dead, but it was really him under that mask, barely standing and covered in blood.

grounded_facts: A climactic confrontation between Sidney, Gale, Dewey, and the Ghostface killers (Roman and Angelina) at the Macher residence, resulting in the exposure of Roman's identity and the defeat of the killers.
memories.memory_text: I was handcuffed and thrown onto the couch at the Macher house, but I broke free and tackled Angelina when she tried to attack; we fought hard, I slammed her head down, she slashed me, but I got her in a headlock and pushed the TV onto her, and after everything, I stood with Sidney and Dewey as we faced the aftermath together.

grounded_facts: Gale frees herself from handcuffs and defeats Angelina in combat, culminating in killing her by dropping a TV on her head.
memories.memory_text: I rolled off the couch, popped the handcuffs, declared 'I know all the tricks!', then tackled Angelina into the coffee table, fought her fiercely—she slashed me, but I slammed her head, got her in a headlock under the TV unit, pushed the TV down on her head, sending electric shocks through her until her body went limp, and even though Sid shot her afterward, I knew I'd already taken her down.

grounded_facts: After both are incapacitated, Sidney shoots Roman in the head and later kills Angelina after she briefly revives.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney shoot Roman in the head after he was already down, and then I watched her kill Angelina when she suddenly came charging out, screaming, and got shot right between the eyes.

grounded_facts: Medical response following the final attack, with Dewey and Gale being treated in an ambulance
memories.memory_text: I was lying on a stretcher in the ambulance, and I reached over to take Dewey's hand as we were being treated.

grounded_facts: Dewey verbally initiates the renewal of their romantic relationship during a vulnerable moment
Dewey asks Gale if they can try their relationship again, citing the moment as meaningful despite the timing.
memories.memory_text: I remember Dewey turning to me and asking if we could try our relationship again, saying he knew it was a bad time but wanted to give it another shot.

grounded_facts: Gale expresses gratitude for Dewey saving her life and agrees to restart their relationship
Gale agrees to give her relationship with Dewey another chance, acknowledging his heroism.
memories.memory_text: I told Dewey, 'Sure, why not. You did save my life, Mr. Rielly,' and I meant it—I was grateful and ready to give us another chance.

grounded_facts: Law enforcement and survivors assess the damage and disengage from the scene after the climax
memories.memory_text: I overheard the officers talking outside, assessing what had happened and saying their goodbyes, while I was still in the ambulance with Dewey.

memories.memory_text: I drove my red BMW through the back lot, the banners for Stab 3 closing in around me—Woodsboro turned into a show, and now I'm the one making sure it feels real.
I was on the Stab 3 set, walking through the fake Woodsboro, when Tom Prinze told me someone iced Ben Damon and his girlfriend—I felt that chill, like the past was rushing back in.

I stared through the two-way mirror, feeling the weight of everything unsaid between Gale and me, and finally let the resentment surface when I said those words—'Brace yourself, Gale, all of this is actually not About you'—because after everything, she still doesn't get it.
I told Gale to stop following me, and when she didn’t back off, I pointed out her running engine—she was careless, and that kind of noise could spook whatever was inside.

Jennifer was sobbing in my arms, hysterical, and then she shouted that the killer was picking victims based on the STAB 3 script—Ben Damon first, then his real girlfriend, Sarah Darling’s character, and now her. When Gale asked if she died in the script, I just nodded, because I knew it was true.
I drew my 9mm and told the others I was prepared for anything—then moved toward the door, ready to face whoever was out there.
The power went out right as I reached the door, and when I opened it, Angelina's body fell in—I yelled for everyone to get out the back, fast.
I was running with Jennifer and Gale when the explosion hit—glass and fire everywhere—and I barely made it into the pool before the roof came apart above us.
I told Kincaid I didn't know where Sidney was, and when he pushed me, I asked if that was a threat—then asked again, because I needed to be sure he was crossing the line.

I was on the phone leaving another message for Sid, desperate for her to pick up, when I suddenly saw her turn the corner with a cop—my heart slammed in my chest, half in relief, half in fear because she wasn’t supposed to be here. I held her tight, then snapped, 'What are you doing here? I told you to stay hidden!'

I realized my phone must've been how the killer got Sidney's number—Jennifer and Kincaid both used it, and I had her number saved. That moment hit me like a gut punch, knowing I might’ve accidentally put her in danger.
I saw Karen Colcheck step out suddenly, spooking all of us—Sidney, Gale, and me—and when I recognized her, I said her name and where she was from. Woodsboro.
I asked Gale if she wanted us to come with her, and she shot me down, saying she works better alone.
I asked Sid if she wanted me to come with her, remembering Randy’s rules about never being alone, but she brushed it off with a smile, showing me her mace and knife like it was a joke.

Sidney came running toward me, screaming, and then just collapsed into my arms—shaking, hysterical—after barely escaping that killer on the lot. I held her tight, keeping my gun ready, knowing I had to keep her safe right then.
I looked Milton dead in the eye and said, 'So you knew Sidney Prescott's mother,' watching him shift in his seat like he wanted to bolt.
When he tried to play dumb, I told him I was calling Detective Kincaid—just saying it put the fear in him, and he finally admitted he recognized her during the first 'Stab' movie.

I held my breath as we crept out of that closet, Jennifer gagging the whole time—Gale and I had to snap at her to shut up before she blew our cover. I silenced them both, then moved first into Milton's dark office, knowing one wrong sound could ruin everything.

I bumped heads with Gale while breaking open Milton's locked drawer, and for a second it felt like something old between us came back—then I smashed the lock with my flashlight and she pulled out those paternity results.
I saw the Ghost attacker lunge at us after killing Jennifer, and the only thing I could do was yell 'Gale run!' before I stepped in and got hit in the head with the knife—then everything went black.
I remember the sharp pain in my side, the warmth of blood soaking through my shirt, knowing I couldn't move fast enough to stop what was coming.
I was tied to a chair, beaten and out cold—couldn't move, couldn't speak. The last thing I remember before blacking out was the killer taking my voice, using it to call Sid.
I heard my own voice coming from somewhere—'Help me Sid! The killer's got me!'—and then 'Good work Sid.' It wasn't me. He was using my words like a weapon, and I couldn't stop him.
I burst in, saw Sid, and the first thing I asked was where Gale was — I had to find her, I told Sid to stay put and I’d get her back, I wasn’t letting them take her.
I raised my gun at Ghostface, tried to fire — click, click, nothing. Out of bullets. Then the knife came spinning at me, hit my arm hard, knocked me back — next thing I know, I’m out.
I came out of the laundry room and drove the knife into Roman’s chest just as he was about to get to Sidney—he went flying back and she screamed, but I didn’t stop to see more.
Sidney was shaking and I barely had the strength to stand, but I held her and told her I’d never leave her like that—I could feel her grip tighten like she was afraid I’d vanish again.
I remember the cold metal of the stretcher under me, the flashing lights blurring as they wheeled me out of Sunrise Studios—alive, but barely holding on.
I looked at Gale and said it was a bad time, but asked if we could try the relationship thing again—just put it out there, heart on my sleeve while she held my hand in the ambulance.
She smiled and said yes, called me 'Mr. Rielly'—then we kissed, hard and fast, right there in the ambulance, like we were both letting go of something heavy.

memories.memory_text: I asked Roman Bridger what his favorite scary movie was. He paused, then said, 'my life.' I repeated, 'Your life?'—and he just smiled.

Out of the corner of my eye, I saw someone in a Ghostface costume standing in the shadows by the exit—just watching. I swear he mimed slicing his throat with a shiny blade. Then the commercial break light buzzed, and when I looked back, he was gone.
I remember Kincaid shoving that evidence bag in my face, the article about Maureen Prescott’s murder—her blank stare in that black-and-white photo, like she knew what was coming.
When he flipped it over and I saw 'SIDNEY' written in thick black marker, my stomach dropped—this wasn’t just another copycat thing, it was aimed right at her.
I asked Dewey to work together like we used to, but he just looked at me with that cold stare and walked away, saying Sidney was more important than I ever was.

I saw Sarah Darling’s body go into the bag, and when Kincaid mentioned they had a suspect, I grabbed his shoulders—my hands were shaking a little—and pushed for the name. I could see it in his eyes: he didn’t want to talk, but I knew I could get in.

Wallace called me 'Diane Sawyer' and told me to go investigate bad meat—like I’m some joke—and I snapped back 'Hey, fuck off' before Kincaid shut him down. Then he actually said I was working with him. I couldn’t believe it.
I heard Roman was questioned about calling Sarah Darling. The roommate said it was his voice, and Sarah supposedly named him. Roman denied it, said he was being framed to kill his film.
I told Dewey this has everything to do with me — I was the one who made the Woodsboro story famous, and I’m not letting him shut me out again.
When he said 'this is actually not about you' and stormed off to be with Jennifer, I felt it — all that resentment, and suddenly I wasn’t sure if he ever trusted me at all.
I remember grabbing the script from Jennifer Jolie’s hands, my heart pounding as I read the line—'AND I DIE NAKED?!'—and shouting that it was complete bullshit, furious and humiliated.

I remember Jennifer screaming at me, hysterical, saying the killer is picking victims based on the script—Ben Damon’s girlfriend, Sarah Darling’s character—and realizing, for the first time, this isn’t just a movie anymore, it’s real.
I snapped at Jennifer to stop being a drama queen when Dewey went to answer the door — killers don’t knock, and I wasn’t about to let fear make us stupid.
After the lights went out and Angelina’s body dropped at the door, I heard Jennifer’s phone ring — I told her to answer it, but I already knew this wasn’t over.
I remember the blast throwing us through the air—glass shattering, the roof tearing apart—and then hitting the cold water of the pool, choking on chlorine as debris crashed around us.

I snapped at Kincaid when he said there were only four victims—he clearly hadn’t done his homework, and I wasn’t going to let him misrepresent the body count when I knew Angelina Tyler was definitely dead too.
I hugged Sidney—actually hugged her—instead of trading insults like usual. For once, it wasn't a fight, it was... relief.
I remembered Dewey’s phone had Sidney’s number stored—I said 'Phone memory!' and it clicked: the killer must’ve seen it when he used the phone.

I remember this goth girl, Karen, lunging out of nowhere with a videotape—scared the hell out of all of us. When Dewey said she was Randy’s ex, I just blurted, 'Who’s this,' because I had no idea who she was, but then she held up that tape like it meant something big.
I told Dewey and Sidney I’d meet up with them later—I work better alone, and they should check the set while I follow my own lead.

I was trying to pick the lock with my credit cards, just like I’ve done before—smiling at the sign saying 'AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY' like it didn’t apply to me—when suddenly a hand grabbed me from behind and I screamed my god, I actually screamed.
Jennifer showed up, said she’d follow me from now on, and used a key card to get into the building. She said 'Gale Weathers would find a way,' then walked in. I followed.

I led Jennifer down that dark hallway, her whining about basements just proving how out of her depth she was—God, I loved getting under her skin, especially when she muttered 'bitch' like I wouldn’t hear her.
I slapped a twenty on the desk, thinking it might be enough to get us in—Bianca just looked insulted and shoved it back like I was some amateur.
I flipped open the folder and saw those headshots—Maureen Prescott, younger, staring back at me like she had something to hide. 'Rina Reynolds'? What a ridiculous stage name.
I read the list of films—'Amazombies', 'Space Psychos'—and couldn't believe it. B-movies from John Milton? That name hit like a lightning bolt. This wasn't just a scandal—it was a horror show.

I stared Milton down, demanding he admit he knew Rina Reynolds—Sidney’s mother—and when he finally cracked, I could see the guilt in his eyes, even if he tried to hide it behind that smug studio exec bullshit.

When I pushed him on what really happened to Maureen in the 70s, he finally spilled—those so-called parties, the casting favors, the way she was used and discarded—justifying it like it was some twisted game she chose to lose.
I told Jennifer Milton’s not a killer, just a pervert with jack-off parties and his two best friends—then had to spell it out when she didn’t get the joke. His hands, not Reiner and Tarantino.
We crept out of that coat closet in the dark, me and Dewey hushing Jennifer’s gagging, then slipped into Milton’s office while Dewey cracked the door—felt like a damn horror movie heist.
I hit the elevator button and the door opened — Milton was hanging there, split open from chest to crotch, guts piled on the floor. I couldn't even breathe, just screamed until my throat tore.
I saw the killer charging at me, so I faked a move into the elevator and then tripped him as he rushed past — he went down hard, face first, and I bolted for the stairs.
I saw Kincaid spin around when that voice hit, then the Ghost just came out of nowhere and slashed his throat—blood sprayed across the hood of the car, and he just dropped.
The killer told me not to run, said I'd end up skewered like a pig, and then said he needed me as bait for Sidney—I froze, closed my eyes, and just started crying as he came toward me.
Sidney got the gag off and was untying me—hurry, because that lunatic was coming.
One second we were running for the door, the next—KERSMASH—the Ghost came flying through the window like some demented stuntman, and we barely made it out.
A knife exploded through the door right beside my face—I felt the splinter spray my skin and I screamed before I even knew what happened.
Right after the door was kicked in, another Ghost popped out of that body bag and had a knife to my throat before I could even turn around.
I remember leaning over Dewey on the stretcher, holding his hand—his voice was weak but serious when he asked if we could try the relationship thing again.
I smiled and said 'Sure, why not'—then we kissed like we were trying to prove we were still alive.
