memories.memory_text: I saw my mom’s ghost at the window, her face pressed against the glass, lips moving like she was trying to tell me something—I couldn’t hear her, but I felt it in my chest, like she was pulling me toward her.

The glass exploded inward as a figure smashed through it—my mom was gone, just streaks of blood on the window, and then that thing lunged at me; I screamed and woke up, heart pounding, Pete still barking like it was real.
The voice on the phone knew my real name—Sidney—and brought up my mother, Maureen Prescott, like it was some kind of sick punchline. I felt my breath catch, tears burning before I could stop them.

He threatened Dewey, said he had his eyes on him like he was next, and told me to come to Hollywood—my hands shook so bad I ripped the headset out and grabbed my gun, staring into that dark night like it might swallow me whole.
I'm speeding down this empty highway in my Honda, the dark stretching on forever—can't think, just drive, just get away.
I can't stop my thumbs from tapping on the wheel, the silence pressing in even with that creepy song playing, and I don't realize how fast I'm going until the road blurs.
I wasn't there, but Dewey said my name like I was still in the crosshairs—like the past was still breathing down my neck.
I turned the corner and heard Dewey's voice on the phone, calling me again—six times, he said—and then he saw me. We ran into each other’s arms, and for a second, I didn’t feel alone anymore.
I told him the killer called me last night—that he found me—and I could see the look on his face change. I had to come here because hiding wasn’t keeping me safe anymore.

I watched Randy’s tape and heard him say this wasn’t just another sequel—it was the end of a trilogy, and everything we thought was true might not be. When he said the past would come back to destroy us, I felt it like a punch, like he was warning me about something buried deep.
I hugged Karen goodbye, told her to be careful, and watched her run off like nothing had ever happened—same old Karen, always chasing the next thing.

I told Dewey I had to go to the bathroom, and even though he offered to come with me, I said no—I’ve got my mace, my knife, and these two fists. I remember raising them up, half-smiling, like I was joking, but I meant it.

I was drying my face when I heard it—'Siiiiiddney'—a whisper, like it was playing tricks, but then I knew someone was really there. I pulled my gravity knife, crouched low, scanning the stalls, heart pounding, but saw no feet—just the AC rumbling, making me second-guess until that stall door exploded open.
I came around the corner, saw the dead end, and then the door exploded open—he was right behind me. I barely made it over the fence with his knife stabbing through the wood where I just was.

I was still shaking in Dewey's arms when Gale and Jennifer showed up, talking about my mom being an actress and John Milton being involved—I couldn't process it, not after what just happened in the bathroom.

I sat there looking at those Hollywood script books, and when Kincaid said he sees ghosts too, I realized I’ve been watching my life like a movie—like I’m learning who my mother was, and who I am, through all this madness.

After Kincaid leaned in and whispered that his life is his favorite scary movie, I sat alone for a beat and then said it too—mine too—because I finally felt someone else understood the horror I live in every day.
I heard the killer say he needed Gale as bait for me—his voice was cold, deliberate, and it sent a jolt through me, knowing I was the target he was hunting.
I picked up the phone and heard my own voice echoing back at me—cold, distorted—then that voice saying, 'I only her you too, Sidney,' and my stomach dropped because I knew they had Gale and Dewey.
After the call ended, I stood there shaking, then saw Wallace's keys on the desk—hesitated—then opened his drawer and found the gun. I didn't think. I just took it. That's the ticket.
I was driving fast through the rain when my phone rang, and that voice told me to go to Sunrise Studios—it felt like he was directing me like a damn character in his sick movie.
I parked Wallace's car by the studio gates, climbed onto the hood, and started scaling the iron fence—my hands gripped the cold metal as I pulled myself over, knowing there was no turning back.

I crept through the dark lot, phone in hand, and when I answered, that voice told me to finish this where it all began—Woodsboro—but I was standing right there, staring at that giant Stab 3 poster with the Ghost figure looming over me, knife raised, and I knew this was it.

I stepped onto the set, and everything looked exactly how I remembered—too still, too familiar. Then my phone rang, and I just said it straight: 'Alright I'm here, now show your face so we can finish this.'
I saw Kincaid’s body hanging there—real, not foam like in the movie. I flinched, covered my eyes. I couldn’t unsee it, but I kept walking.
I heard Dewey's voice on the phone, desperate—'Help me Sid! The killer's got me!'—and when I ran outside, I saw him tied up, beaten, barely moving. My heart stopped. This couldn't be real.

After dropping the phone, I turned and saw Ghostface standing there with that box—he clicked it and suddenly I heard my own voice say, 'You play a good game Sidney,' then it shifted to my mother's voice saying, 'Your other half.' I screamed and ran.
I found Gale tied to the bed, her mouth gagged, eyes wide with fear—I could see she was screaming at me to hurry before I even got close.
After freeing Gale, I saw the Ghost crash through the window and screamed 'GALE WATCHOUT!' as we ran for the door.

I fired at the door, three shots—BLAM! BLAM! BLAM!—and for a second, it went quiet. Then the body bag on the bed unzipped and another Ghost appeared. I tried to raise the gun again, but the door exploded open and the first killer slammed into me, knocking the gun out of my hands.

I didn't think—I just ran for the window and jumped. Glass shattered all around me as I crashed through, then I was falling, landing hard on the awning before rolling onto the grass. I lay there dazed, blinking up and seeing the Ghost's face staring down at me through the broken window frame.
I saw Dewey stumble through the doorway and I ran to him — for a second, I actually felt safe again, like maybe we could stop this nightmare together.
I turned after locking the door and saw Angelina's body at my feet — then her eyes snapped open, that twisted smile spreading as she raised a gun straight at my face.

I heard that voice, cold and familiar, saying I wasn't going anywhere — then he tore off the Ghostface mask and it was Roman. He just stood there, calm, calling himself my brother, saying Mom had shut him out, that she was my mother but not his, not really.
He said he directed everything — even Angelina, smiling like it was all a show — and that he made a 'home movie' after Mom turned him away, like my entire trauma was just footage for his sick film.
I walked through the studio gates with the morning sun rising overhead, calm and steady, like nothing had happened—like I was finally free.
